title: All-Hands April 2026 - Talking Points & Q&A (Draft)
content:
Goal:
- Clear 20-minute exec update + 10-minute product/demo + 15-minute live Q&A.
- Make progress feel tangible: what we shipped, what customers are saying, and what’s next.
- Avoid deep technical detail; highlight product impact and operational wins.

Key messages (draft):
1) Product momentum: Redwood Dedicated GA metrics and early enterprise signups. Quick numbers to call out: two pilot contracts closed, avg latency improvements on core models ~15-20% vs baseline. (Confirm exact figures with Eng before final.)
2) Reliability & scaling: SRE/infra wins (99.95% last month on hosted API; incident mean time to recovery improved). Shout-out to on-call rotation changes.
3) Private & compliance progress: pilot deployments progressing; first on-prem customer demo scheduled for late April.
4) Hiring & org health: small hiring push in infra and solutions eng; retention update and people programs.
5) Roadmap teaser: focus areas for next quarter — autoscaling improvements, rollout tooling for model versioning, Optimize beta.

Talking points (speaker notes):
- Opening (CEO / Headline): 30s — quick celebration (wins) + framing for the quarter.
- Product demo (PM): 8-10min — show Dedicated dashboard, rollout canary, and failure/fallback demo. Keep it simple, emphasize the customer benefit (predictable latency/cost).
- Engineering shout-outs (Eng lead): 2-3min — call out KV cache improvement and kernel selection improvements (again, confirm safe wording).
- GTM/customer highlight (CS): 1-2min — short customer quote or win; mention industries (finserv/reghealth) without naming PII.
- Close & invite to Q&A (People Ops): logistics for post-meeting office hours and AMA.

Demo checklist (for PM/Eng):
- Pre-record fallback scenario in case live demo is flaky.
- Ensure demo token has correct permissions and does not use real customer data.
- Slides: 3 screenshots + 1 short clip showing console trace and latency metrics.
- Backup: short video of previous demo (2min) stored in Drive link (add link here later).

Draft Q&A (anticipate):
Q: Any updates on pricing changes / usage billing?
A: No immediate pricing changes planned. We continue optimizing unit economics via Optimize and recommend dedicated pricing for high-throughput customers. If asked for specifics, redirect to pricing@redwood-inference and offer follow-up.

Q: How are we managing model quality regressions with new kernels/quantization?
A: We run continuous evals tied to our regression suite; rollouts are canaryed and we have automatic fallback to previous model variants if drift detected. (Keep technical depth light.)

Q: Are we expanding regions / cloud partners?
A: Yes — roadmap includes additional EU and APAC cloud regions in the next two quarters; timeline depends on partner integrations.

Q: Any layoffs / org restructuring?
A: No. We’re hiring in key areas; will notify teams first for org changes. Keep transparent and empathetic.

Parking lot / unanswered / follow-ups:
- Finalize Dedicated GA metrics (Jordan) — need exact latency % improvement and signed pilot customer names (if approved) by 2026-03-10.
- Confirm SLO numbers with SRE (Samir) and whether we can safely state 99.95% for last month.
- Add link to pre-recorded demo video (Maya).
- Draft 1-sheeter for sales describing canary + fallback behavior (Marketing).

Logistics / run of show (draft):
- 11:00 AM — All-hands start (CEO opening)
- 11:02 AM — Product demo (PM)
- 11:12 AM — Engineering update + shout-outs
- 11:15 AM — Customer/CS highlight
- 11:17 AM — People Ops closing + announce AMA (office hours)
- 11:20 AM — Live Q&A (15 min)

Tone notes / communication guidance:
- Stay concise and optimistic; focus on customer impact.
- If asked for specifics we don't want to disclose, say: "We’ll follow up with the team to share details."
- For competitive questions: emphasize our differentiators (unified serving, cost controls, fallback strategies) without naming competitors.

To-dos (owner names):
- Jordan: confirm Dedicated GA metrics (due 2026-03-10).
- Samir: SRE SLO confirmation + one-liner explanation for non-technical audience (due 2026-03-05).
- Maya: upload pre-recorded demo and final slide deck (due 2026-03-08).
- Kai: finalize talking points and circulate to execs for review (due 2026-03-07).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the demo under 10min — attention drops after that.
- Avoid deep dive into kernel/quant details; it bores most non-eng folks.
- Add a short customer quote slide if we can get permission this week.
- Check with Legal on what we can say re: pilot customers (CC legal@redwood-inference).

Unresolved questions (for exec sync):
- Do we want to announce the Optimize beta publicly during AH or save for a dedicated product email? Pros/cons noted below.
- Any specific employee recognition we should include beyond engineering shout-outs?

-- end draft --

(This is a working doc — lots of TODOs and placeholders. Use comments inline or add suggestions in Slack #all-hands.)
